record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: When K(V) contains a diagonalisable Killing tensor with distinct eigenvalues on a constant-curvature space, what kind of tensor is it, and which labelled in-forests from the separation-of-variables classification occur in superintegrable systems?

evidence.quote: Q2 If so, what kind this Ki is? Recall that in the case of constant curvature, a diagonalisable Killing tensor with different eigenvalues leads to separation of variable. Separation of variables on spaces of constant curvature was described in [11], the classifying object is a labeled in-forest F. What labeled in-forests appear within superintegrable systems?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature. A Killing tensor of valence 2 on $(M,g)$ is a symmetric $(2,0)$-tensor field $K$ satisfying $\nabla_{(a}K_{bc)}=0$, where $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection. Denote by $\mathcal{K}(V)$ the space of valence-2 Killing tensors associated with a (super)integrable natural Hamiltonian system $H=\tfrac12 g^{ab}p_a p_b + V(x)$ on $T^*M$, i.e., symmetric tensors $K$ such that $F=K^{ab}p_a p_b + U(x)$ Poisson-commutes with $H$ for some function $U$.

It is classical that a diagonalisable Killing tensor with pointwise distinct eigenvalues on a constant-curvature space induces an orthogonal separation of variables for the Hamilton–Jacobi equation of $H$, and the set of equivalence classes of such separating structures on constant-curvature spaces is in bijection with a combinatorial classifying object: a labelled in-forest $F$ (a rooted forest with vertices carrying labels encoding the block structure of the associated Stäckel coordinates).

Assume that $\mathcal{K}(V)$ contains a diagonalisable Killing tensor $K$ with pointwise distinct eigenvalues. 

(a) Characterise the tensor $K$: describe the geometric/algebraic type of $K$ that arises in this situation (e.g., its relation to the metric and to Benenti-type or characteristic Killing tensors).

(b) Determine which labelled in-forests $F$, from the classification of orthogonal separation of variables on constant-curvature spaces, can occur as the separation structure of a (maximally) superintegrable natural Hamiltonian system on a space of constant curvature.
artifact.category_tag: Killing tensors and separation of variables
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research problem connecting Nijenhuis geometry, separation of variables, and superintegrability. While the orthogonal separation of variables on constant curvature spaces has been classified (e.g., via labelled in-forests / Stäckel coordinates), no source found provides a complete characterization of which labelled in-forests are realised by superintegrable systems, nor a definitive identification of the diagonalisable Killing tensor with distinct eigenvalues arising in $\mathcal{K}(V)$ for superintegrable systems. Recent work (e.g., torsion-free connections of maximally superintegrable systems, 2024) addresses related structural aspects but does not resolve this classification.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonal separation of variables for spaces of constant curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs all orthogonal separating coordinates in constant curvature spaces of arbitrary signature with explicit Killing tensors and Stäckel matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the classification background for orthogonal separation on constant curvature spaces but does not classify which labelled in-forests arise specifically in superintegrable systems.

status_evidence.title: Torsion-free connections of second-order maximally superintegrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies primary/secondary structure tensors of second-order maximally superintegrable systems and their induced torsion-free connections.
status_evidence.claim: Recent related work on the geometry of superintegrable systems, but does not resolve the in-forest classification question.
